fields.h1: Build a Piercing Consent Form That Records Every Piercing
fields.hero_description: Build a piercing consent form that logs each piercing's placement and jewelry and saves the signed record to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Piercer Needs on the Signed Form
fields.features_subheading: Every piercing in a visit gets its own line, and the whole visit sits on one record the front desk can pull up by name.
fields.feature_1:
A line for each piercing in the visit

List the placement, jewelry style, material, and gauge for every piercing the client gets today. A helix and a nostril done in one visit become two lines on a single signed record.
fields.feature_2:
Date of birth before anything else

Ask for date of birth and a photo of a government ID first. A client under 18 sees a parent section with its own ID upload, and the signature box stays locked until it is filled.
fields.feature_3:
Health questions the piercer sees first

Ask about metal allergies, blood thinners, and pregnancy as plain yes or no questions. Any yes marks the record, so the piercer reads those answers before laying out the jewelry.
fields.feature_4:
Signatures on a tablet or a phone

Clients sign with a finger on the counter tablet or on their own phone from a booking email. The app keeps that signature on the same record as every answer the client gave.
fields.feature_5:
Records you can pull by piercer or month

Every signed form lands as a row in a database the studio owns, filed under the client's name and the piercer's. Filter by one piercer and one month to see every piercing they did.
fields.feature_6:
The full source, exported to your GitHub

On paid plans, export the code to your GitHub repository and host the form on the studio's own website. A developer picks it up from there and keeps building, with no rebuild.

fields.usecase_heading: How Piercing Studios Use the Form
fields.tab_content_1:
Three piercings, signed for on a single record

Saturdays at Bluegill Piercing bring a line at the counter. Corin Abbott signs on the counter tablet for 3 piercings: a helix, a forward helix, and a nostril. Each piercing gets its own line with its jewelry and gauge. One signature covers the visit, and the piercer, Harlow Vance, sees all 3 lines before setting up.
fields.tab_content_2:
For a minor, a parent signs in person

Junebug Piercing in Pensacola asks each client's age first. When 15-year-old Ivy Fenwick books a nostril piercing, a parent section opens. Her mother, Nadia Fenwick, uploads photo ID and the notarized consent, then signs. Florida wants notarized consent for any minor, and a parent present under 16.
fields.tab_content_3:
Metal allergy answers that the piercer reads first

Talia Brandt checks yes to a nickel allergy on her form at Ember Row Piercing. Her record is flagged, and the piercers channel in Slack gets a message that a new form is in, with a link. The allergy answer itself stays in the database. Jonah Ruiz opens the record and talks through jewelry with her first.
fields.tab_content_4:
Downsizes that stay with the first piercing

Six weeks after her helix piercing, Marlo Keane returns to Bluegill Piercing for a downsize. The piercer finds her original record by name and logs the visit under that helix, with the bar going from 8 mm to 6 mm. The record now shows both visits, and Marlo gets an email with her aftercare sheet for the new bar.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Piercing Consent Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a piercing consent form that logs every piercing and handles minors, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Give each piercing its own line
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Put the age question on screen one
fields.howto_step_1_des: Read your state's body piercing statute and your county health department's rules before you write a question. Note the minimum age, what a parent must sign or bring, and what each visit record has to hold. Florida's list includes the area pierced and the piercer's name.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down the questions your piercers ask before every appointment: metal allergies, blood thinners, pregnancy, skin conditions near the site, and whether the client has eaten. Phrase each as yes or no, and mark which answers should flag the record.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Set up a repeating line for each piercing. A client getting three piercings fills in three lines, with the jewelry details for each. Add the piercer's name to every line, because two piercers can share one visit.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask for date of birth on the first screen. For clients under 18, show a parent section with the parent's photo ID, an upload for any notarized consent your state requires, and a second signature line.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your questions and consent wording into a prompt and describe the form in plain English. Emergent builds the form and the database table of signed records, and you change any part of it by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Choose who hears about new forms
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick where a new form is announced: a piercers channel in Slack, or an email to the front desk. Keep the message to the client's name and a link to the record, and leave the health answers in the database.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it as two different clients
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in the form yourself twice, once as a 15-year-old with a parent and once as an adult getting two piercings, then open both records. Ask a local attorney to review the consent and release wording before the tablet goes on the counter.

faq_plan.q: What is on a piercing consent form?
faq_plan.ref: What is on a piercing consent form?

prov.original: What is on a piercing consent form?

faq_plan.a: It holds who the client is and each piercing they agreed to, with its placement and jewelry. It also carries yes or no health answers and the client's signature, plus a parent section for a minor. Florida's statute, for one, has studios record the date of visit and the area pierced, along with the name of the person performing the piercing.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a piercing consent form?
faq_plan.a: List the questions your piercers ask, paste in your consent wording, and describe the form to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English. Emergent turns that prompt into the form and a database of signed records, and another prompt changes either one. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: How do I adapt a piercing consent form template to my studio?
faq_plan.a: Replace its generic questions with the ones your own piercers ask. A piercing consent form template knows nothing about your jewelry list or the age rules in your state. Describe those details in a plain-English prompt, and Emergent builds the form around them.

faq_plan.q: Is a free piercing consent form enough for a busy studio?
faq_plan.a: It covers the signature, but not finding the record later. A free piercing consent form on paper ends up in a binder, one sheet per client. Studios that also do lashes keep a lash extension consent form in a second binder. A form built with Emergent has no response caps, however many walk-ins sign.

faq_plan.q: What happens if a client adds another piercing after signing the consent form?
faq_plan.a: Have the client sign again for the new piercing. Add it as a new line on the same visit record, with its own placement and jewelry, and capture a second signature that covers only that line. The record then shows what was agreed before the first needle and what was added after.

faq_plan.q: Does ear lobe piercing need the same consent form as body piercing?
faq_plan.a: Not always. It depends on your state and the method. Florida's statute, for one, leaves a mechanized, presterilized ear-piercing system that penetrates the outer perimeter or lobe of the ear out of its definition of body piercing. Read your own state's definition, then decide whether lobe clients get the full form or a shorter one.

faq_plan.q: How long should a studio keep signed piercing consent forms?
faq_plan.a: Keep each record at least as long as your state requires. Florida's statute sets a period of not less than 2 years for each customer visit record. Ask your attorney or insurer whether to keep them longer. A studio that also offers laser services can store each laser hair removal consent form in its own table next to the piercing records.

faq_plan.q: What should a parent fill in on a piercing consent form for a minor?
faq_plan.a: The parent fills in their name, their relationship to the client, a photo ID, and their own signature. Ask for proof of guardianship when the adult is not a parent. Then check your state's statute for whether the consent must be notarized and whether the parent has to stay for the piercing.

faq_plan.q: Can clients sign a piercing consent form before they arrive?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Send the link in the booking confirmation so the client fills it in at home, then match the photo ID to the person at the counter. A piercing consent form PDF would need printing first. The app Emergent builds can capture an e-signature on the client's phone. Ask your attorney whether e-signatures meet your state's rules.

faq_plan.q: Should a piercing consent form include aftercare instructions?
faq_plan.a: Yes, or it should record that the client received them. Florida's statute tells studios to provide each customer with written instructions on the proper care of the pierced area. Keep the aftercare sheet specific to the service: a studio that also offers injectables pairs a botox consent form with its own instructions, not the piercing sheet.
